To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the loss of tetracycline from fetal rat bone in organ cultures is greater than that of calcium.
bone growth and bone resorption are accompanied by different losses of3H- and45Ca-labeled minerals from the calcified portions of bones in organ culture.
fetal rat bones in culture release more3H-tyrtracycline than45Cawhen the bones are growing and that more of both isotopes are released when the bones are atrophying.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which bone growth and bone resorption are regulated in the fetus.
the mechanisms by which bone is formed and destroyed, and the factors that control these processes.
the mechanisms by which the skeleton is maintained in the growing animal and the mechanisms by which it is remodeled during the aging process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in the fetal rat bones studied in vitro, bone growth is accompanied by a greater loss of3H-tacracycline than of bone calcium, whereas in bone atrophy, bone calcium is conserved and lost at the same rate as the bone collagen.
the loss of45Ca and of3H-tyr was greater during resorption than during growth and was similar in amount in the two conditions.
the results of this study are consistent with the hypothesis that bone resorption during bone growth is not the same as bone resorption during atrophy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the loss of45Ca from the calcified portions of the bones is not related to the rate of bone growth or bone atrophy, but the loss of3H-tracycline is related to the rate.

bone growth is a dynamic process that is associated with the loss of bone collagen, bone matrix and bone mineral, and that bone atrophy is associated with a similar loss of bone mineral and bone matrix, but not of bone collagen.
bone growth is accompanied by local retention of45Ca, but not of3H-tyr, and that bone atrophy is accompanied by the release of both45Ca and3HTyr.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bone growth and bone resorption are two different phenomena.
the amount of3H-tyr was significantly lower in the group of patients with a high risk of developing type 2 diabetes than that of patients without diabetes.
the bone loss during the resorption of fetal rat bones in organ culture is different from the bone loss in vivo during the resorption accompanying growth.
